Task: rank the five most likely patients, most likely first, with a probability for each (they need not sum to one). For each, say which findings in the report support the placement and which argue against it, counting recorded absences as evidence; keep each to one or two sentences. Then say what the report lacked that would have made you more confident.

ranking.for: Exhibits the core triad of KLHL20-related disorder including seizures, myoclonus, EEG abnormalities, behavioral abnormalities (ADHD), mild intellectual disability, and characteristic facial dysmorphism including a high/prominent forehead.
ranking.against: Microcephaly and lower limb spasticity are not consistently emphasized as cardinal findings in available KLHL20 summaries.

ranking.for: Presents with early-onset seizures, intellectual disability, global developmental delay, EEG abnormality, and autistic behavior.
ranking.against: Broad forehead and an extensive list of typical craniofacial dysmorphic features are explicitly recorded as absent.

ranking.for: Exhibits early multiple seizure types (tonic-clonic, absence, myoclonic) alongside intellectual disability and developmental delay.
ranking.against: Behavioral abnormalities (autistic and aggressive behavior) and EEG abnormalities are explicitly recorded as absent.

ranking.for: Displays seizures, autistic behavior, and global developmental delay.
ranking.against: Facial dysmorphism is not documented, while non-specific structural defects (ventricular septal defect, hydronephrosis) are present.

ranking.for: Features prominent behavioral abnormalities (autism, hyperactivity, aggressive behavior), intellectual disability, and facial dysmorphisms.
ranking.against: Lacks any reported history of early-onset seizures or epilepsy, which is a core hallmark of KLHL20-related disorder.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: The report lacked detailed descriptions of the full spectrum of dysmorphic facial features and explicit seizure semiologies/ages of onset associated with KLHL20 variants beyond the brief mention of prominent forehead and early-onset seizures.

ranking.for: Demonstrates the complete characteristic triad of intellectual disability/developmental disorder, seizures with EEG abnormality, behavioral problems (ADHD), and facial dysmorphisms specifically cited in KLHL20 phenotypes (prominent/high forehead and downslanted palpebral fissures).
ranking.against: Displays features such as lower limb spasticity and enlarged cisterna magna which are not explicitly detailed in the brief clinical summary.

ranking.for: Features intellectual disability, autistic behavior, and early childhood seizures (bilateral tonic-clonic with focal onset and EEG abnormality).
ranking.against: Has an extensive list of recorded absent facial dysmorphic features (including broad forehead) and presents with intraventricular hemorrhage and cerebellar vermis atrophy.

ranking.for: Presents with mild intellectual disability, global developmental delay, and multiple seizure types (myoclonic, absence, bilateral tonic-clonic).
ranking.against: Behavioral abnormalities such as autistic behavior and aggression are documented as absent, along with a documented absence of EEG abnormalities and specific facial features.

ranking.for: Displays global developmental delay, seizures, and autistic behavioral abnormalities.
ranking.against: Lacks the characteristic facial dysmorphisms and exhibits congenital organ anomalies (ventricular septal defect, hydronephrosis) not highlighted as core manifestations of KLHL20 disorder.

ranking.for: Shows intellectual disability, expressive language delay, facial dysmorphisms, and prominent behavioral features (autistic behavior, hyperactivity, aggressive behavior).
ranking.against: Lacks any reported history of early-onset seizures or epilepsy, which is a hallmark feature of the condition.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: A comprehensive delineation of specific facial dysmorphic signs beyond prominent forehead (such as palpebral fissure slant or lip morphology), details on seizure semiology/age at onset, and exact behavioral spectra associated with KLHL20 variants.

ranking.for: Demonstrates all core domains of the disorder: early-onset seizures with EEG abnormalities, behavioral abnormalities (ADHD), intellectual disability, and characteristic facial dysmorphism including a high/prominent forehead.
ranking.against: Microcephaly and lower limb spasticity are not highlighted in the primary disease synopsis.

ranking.for: Features early-onset bilateral tonic-clonic seizures, intellectual disability, EEG abnormality, and behavioral abnormalities (autistic behavior).
ranking.against: Lacks the characteristic facial dysmorphisms, with broad forehead, coarse features, and numerous facial markers explicitly recorded as absent.

ranking.for: Presents with childhood-onset epilepsy involving multiple seizure types, global developmental delay, and mild intellectual disability.
ranking.against: Behavioral abnormalities (autistic behavior, aggressive behavior) are documented as absent, and facial dysmorphic features are largely absent.

ranking.for: Shows global developmental delay, seizures, and behavioral abnormalities (autistic behavior).
ranking.against: Lacks documented characteristic facial features and has congenital systemic anomalies (ventricular septal defect, hydronephrosis) not typical of KLHL20.

ranking.for: Displays marked behavioral abnormalities (autistic behavior, hyperactivity, aggression) and intellectual disability.
ranking.against: Seizures—a cardinal and namesake feature of this condition—are notably not reported.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: The report lacked detailed clinical descriptions of the specific facial gestalt (beyond isolated features like a prominent forehead) and exact seizure semiology/age of onset for KLHL20-related disorder.
